_source.dataset: LA County block-group typical home values from Assessor base-year resets
_source.publisher: Los Angeles County Assessor (public parcel layer)
_source.method: Single-family parcels (UseCode 0100, Units1 = 1) whose land and improvement base years are equal and in 2022-2026, on the 2026 roll, assigned to 2020 block groups by their centroid (CENTER_LAT/LON) inside the block-group polygons of app/data/bundle-la.b64.txt. Excluded: homes built or rebuilt (effective year) in or after the year before their base year (possible new-construction reassessments), land under $50k or improvements under $20k, living area under 400 sq ft, total over $20M. Per block group: median of land + improvement value, median value per living sq ft, count and base-year span. Block groups with fewer than 5 homes fall back to their tract (at least 5 homes), else no value.

legal_basis.text: Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code §110.1(a)-(b): the base year value is the fair market value on the date a purchase or change in ownership occurs (or new construction is completed). §110(b): on a purchase, full cash value is the purchase price paid, rebuttably presumed so for an arm's-length transaction.
legal_basis.note: Read from california.public.law (a reproduction of the code); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov blocked automated access.

proxy_caveats: A base-year reset is a proxy for a sale: some are non-sale changes in ownership reassessed at the Assessor's appraisal (e.g. Prop 19 transfers).
Values are on the 2026 roll, so older base years include annual inflation factors of up to 2% a year.
_source.format: bg / tract: GEOID -> [homes, median value $, median $ per living sq ft, first base year, last base year]

model.name: la_assessor_resets_regression
model.description: Least squares on log value with cross-fitted neighborhood features (a home is never in its own neighborhood statistics while fitting), intercept shifted by the median residual so it targets the typical home.

tested.protocol: Model chosen on 2024 resets using statistics from 2022-23 (dev); locked; then tested once on 2025-26 resets using statistics from 2022-24. No test home appears in the training data or in its own neighborhood statistics.

model.production_note: The page applies these coefficients with neighborhood statistics from 2022-26 resets (the file's bg/tract tables), one year fresher than the tested configuration.

verification.method: Machine-built from the saved public-record pulls (every query is listed in _source.pulls); re-run the script to reproduce.
verification.evidence: 150596 homes; 6029 block groups and 2334 tracts with at least one home
verification.notes: Verified means the medians are computed from the public records as stated; the base-year values remain a proxy for sale prices.
